transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connell (Redwood CS), Sofia Ramos (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Brightwave Procurement), Leah Ortiz (Brightwave Legal), Omar Singh (Brightwave CTO), Marta Lopez (Brightwave InfoSec), Priya Patel (Brightwave Vendor Risk)

Auto-generated summary (may contain errors): Discussed MSA/DPA redlines and proposed SLA remediation path -- intent to provide single page SLA remediation and annotated contract excerpt.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining on a late Monday afternoon, appreciate it. I'm Jordan Hayes, AE at Redwood. I'll hand to Priya for the technical framing in a second. Quick roll call?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Daniel): This is Daniel Kim, Head of Procurement at Brightwave. Hi.
00:14 Speaker 3 (Leah): Leah Ortiz, legal counsel. Hello.
00:18 Speaker 4 (Omar): Omar Singh, CTO.
00:21 Speaker 5 (Marta): Marta Lopez, InfoSec.
00:23 Speaker 6 (Priya P): Priya Patel, vendor risk.
00:25 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Great. Priya, over to you for the tech overview?
00:29 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Thanks Jordan. Hi all, Priya Nair, solutions engineering. We'll do a quick framing on SLA tiers and then jump into the contract exceptions that Leah sent earlier. Apologies in advance, I have the notes in front of me and might read bits.
00:45 Speaker 7 (Priya N): From Redwood's side, two main deployment modes to consider for production workloads: Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem). Hosted API is an option but for PHI-like workloads we typically recommend Private or Dedicated with encryption-at-rest and KMS integration.
01:05 Speaker 4 (Omar): Quick question, the DPA -- is the KMS per-tenant or shared? The wording in the stub DPA seemed ambiguous.
01:11 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Right now we support both customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, and Redwood-managed keys for hosted. We'll note that in the DPA excerpt.
01:20 Speaker 3 (Leah): The two primary redlines from legal: 1) indemnity cap clarification re: PHI and 2) data residency + subcontractor list. We also flagged audit rights timing.
01:34 Speaker 2 (Daniel): From procurement, we're more focused on SLA exposure. If we accept the hosted fallback, how does the console show us failover events and are there credits?
01:44 Speaker 7 (Priya N): We have logging and audit trail but credit policy is mostly governed by SLA language — typically credits scale with downtime percentage per month. For Dedicated we have stronger uptime targets and higher credits.
01:58 Speaker 1 (Jordan): To be concrete, we propose an SLA remediation plan: immediate: adjust MSA language to include explicit fallback tiers (Hosted <-> Dedicated <-> Private) with transparency on routing and logging; medium: define error budget and credits; long: propose a pilot with strict availability windows. We'll put that on paper.
02:22 Speaker 5 (Marta): For InfoSec, two red flags: subcontractor/processor list not current, and encryption key custody language ambiguous. We need to see SOC 2 + KMS integration docs.
02:34 Speaker 7 (Priya N): We'll bundle SOC2 certs and the KMS integration note. They are in the trust center link which Jordan will share after the call.
02:41 Speaker 3 (Leah): One nuance: our legal team wants a carveout where PHI-related liability isn't constrained by the same cap.
02:48 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Understood. We can push that up to our legal ops. Typical ask is to carve out certain liabilities; Redwood legal has accepted industry-standard carveouts in other customers but we'd need to surface specifics.
03:05 Speaker 2 (Daniel): On pricing approval: what is the path for reserved capacity? Does signing a reserved quote lock the rest of procurement?
03:12 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Reserved capacity is contractually a monthly/annual commit. We can produce a chart showing unit economics (tokens per dollar) at different reserves. We'll also show the burst capacity behavior.
03:27 Speaker 4 (Omar): Technical deep-dive: we need clarity on latency SLOs for 2k token sequences under load and what our fallback is if GPU pool is exhausted.
03:38 Speaker 7 (Priya N): For 2k seqs, on Dedicated we target p95 < 350ms under normal load for the typical model family; we'll quantify per-model in the remediation doc. If pool exhausted, requests route to fallback model instances with degraded latency but preserved semantics; that's in the routing policy.
03:58 Speaker 6 (Priya P): Any E2E encryption for in-flight between customer's VPC and Redwood when using Private? Need diagram.
04:05 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Yes, Private uses TLS + optional VPN/IPSec, and we can add a diagram to the packet we send.
04:12 Speaker 1 (Jordan): I'm going to pause — I see Leah has posted a few specific redlines in the chat, is now a good time to go through them?
04:18 Speaker 3 (Leah): Yes let's go item by item. I'll read the first one: "Section 9: Indemnification — remove general cap as it applies to breach of PHI."
04:30 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Priya, from a product operations standpoint, do you see any blockers to removing a cap for PHI?
04:35 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Operationally no, but that's a legal/insurance risk question. We need Redwood legal to backup on liability and reinsure if necessary.
04:42 Speaker 3 (Leah): Next redline: "Audit rights — customer requires a 30-day window for on-site or remote audit access annually."
04:50 Speaker 8 (Sofia): We typically offer remote reviews and can negotiate an on-site with appropriate notice. There may be cost-recovery for on-site.
04:58 Speaker 3 (Leah): Also flagged: data residency clause — customers want EU-only processing for EU tenant data. Can Redwood absolutely commit?
05:08 Speaker 7 (Priya N): For Dedicated and Private we can pin regions; hosted may have region constraints but we can explore region isolation. We'll document region mapping.
05:20 Speaker 4 (Omar): When you say pin regions, is that multi-AZ or single AZ? We need multi-AZ for resilience.
05:25 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Multi-AZ for Dedicated is standard; Private depends on customer's infra. We'll note that.
05:33 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Procurement needs an explicit decision runway. Our committee meets 2026-01-12. We need final contract terms and pricing before then ideally.
05:42 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Great, that gives us a hard deadline. We'll aim to deliver redlines and the SLA remediation sheet by 2026-01-06 so you have internal review time.
05:51 Speaker 3 (Leah): There's also a subcontractor transparency ask: provide full list of 3rd-party processors and whether they have access to raw content or only aggregated telemetry.
06:02 Speaker 7 (Priya N): We can provide a processor list and access model; typically only Redwood ops have access to raw payloads under strict logging, and customers on Private keep payloads in their VPC.
06:15 Speaker 5 (Marta): Can you switch to the mitigation playbook? If there's an incident, how will we be notified and what's the RTO vs RPO?
06:25 Speaker 9 (Liam): Hi all, Liam O'Connell from CS. For incidents we have tiered notifications: page for Sev1, email for Sev2, and the console posts incident notes. RTO and RPO vary by deployment — we'll put a small table in the remediation doc.
06:42 Speaker 4 (Omar): I want explicit wording about fallbacks: if Dedicated goes down we do not want automatic failover to hosted without opt-in. Can we make failover opt-in per route?
06:54 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Yes, routing is policy based and can be configured per route; opt-in behavior can be captured in the service level section or the appendix.
07:06 Speaker 3 (Leah): Another legal point: escrow of critical code or model weights in case of termination? Is that on the table?
07:15 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Model weights typically are not escrowed, but for Private deployments customers own their model artifacts. We can discuss a preservation agreement if absolutely necessary.
07:28 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Pricing clarifications: for reserved capacity, do credits apply retroactively if availability breaches occur multiple times in a month?
07:38 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Typically credits scale per month and are applied to the subsequent invoice per contract. We'll put explicit examples in the SLA sheet.
07:48 Speaker 5 (Marta): For us, encryption keys must be customer-controlled for PHI. Can DPA require that?
07:55 Speaker 7 (Priya N): For Private and Dedicated, yes customer-managed KMS is supported, we'll call that out. For hosted we can discuss HSM options but it's more limited.
08:08 Speaker 3 (Leah): On limitation of liability, we're also asking for a higher cap for critical data incidents. Is there flexibility?
08:15 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll take that to Redwood legal; past customers have negotiated higher caps tied to insurance. We'll surface options.
08:25 Speaker 4 (Omar): On technical note, if we want deterministic inference latency, can we carve out a model family and quantization profile? We need guaranteed performance for one workload at minimum.
08:36 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Absolutely — locked model+quant profile on Dedicated is a supported pattern. We'll put that in the pilot proposal.
08:46 Speaker 6 (Priya P): Risk question: subcontractors in APAC. We need to know data center locations and personnel access.
08:55 Speaker 7 (Priya N): We'll include a data center mapping and personnel access summary.
09:03 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Let's get specifics: Leah, can you enumerate the redlines you expect in order of priority?
09:10 Speaker 3 (Leah): Priority one: PHI carveout to indemnity. Two: audit rights window and no more than 5 business days notice for remote logs. Three: data residency and KMS. Four: higher limitation cap for critical incidents. Five: subcontractor transparency.
09:32 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Great. We'll agree to a path: 1) Redwood to send annotated MSA + DPA with suggested language on 2026-01-02, 2) Redwood to send SLA remediation single-sheet on 2026-01-06, 3) follow-up legal sync 2026-01-09 if needed.
09:50 Speaker 2 (Daniel): One more procurement nuance: Brightwave requires procurement to review any addendum that modifies billing cadence. Can you confirm whether reserved capacity changes invoicing frequency?
10:02 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Reserved capacity is typically monthly/annual billing, invoiced per the committment in the quote. We can support monthly amortization plans on larger commits; we'll call that out in the pricing notes.
10:20 Speaker 5 (Marta): Regarding incident notification: do you have a SOC-style runbook we can peek at?
10:28 Speaker 9 (Liam): We have an incident response runbook excerpt we can share; Jordan will put the link in the follow-up.
10:36 Speaker 3 (Leah): Can we get explicit language around data deletion timelines once contract terminates? We need confirmation of 30/90 day processes.
10:45 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Typical is 30 days for shallow deletion and 90 for deeper purging across backups; we'll include specific wording in the DPA draft.
10:56 Speaker 4 (Omar): Does Redwood support real-time audit logs of inference payloads for a rolling 30-day window? That's a must for our debugging.
11:04 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Yes we have logging at the request level and can retain for 30/90/365 depending on contract/price tier. For PHI we recommend Private where you control retention.
11:18 Speaker 2 (Daniel): On the procurement calendar, if we get the redlines on 1/2 and SLA on 1/6, we'll have one week for legal ops review, so the 1/12 committee date is tight but doable.
11:29 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Sounds good. Any blockers preventing Redwood from sending the artifacts on those dates? Priya? Legal?
11:38 Speaker 7 (Priya N): On our side, no blockers operationally. Redwood legal will need 48 hours to review any novel indemnity asks but we can escalate.
11:45 Speaker 8 (Sofia): We'll prepare the single-page SLA remediation and include a table for availability targets, credits, and routing policy.
11:55 Speaker 3 (Leah): Also propose a wording for 'opt-in failover' so we can avoid unwanted routing to hosted.
12:02 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll propose appendix language for opt-in per route and default behavior.
12:10 Speaker 4 (Omar): On the pricing side, will there be a one-time onboarding fee for Private? We need to factor that into procurement.
12:18 Speaker 7 (Priya N): There is typically an onboarding/engineering retainer for Private or on-prem, we will include a range in the pricing note.
12:26 Speaker 5 (Marta): For security, can you confirm annual pen test schedules and whether customers can mandate a 3rd-party pentest?
12:33 Speaker 9 (Liam): We do annual internal and third-party pentests; customers can request a point-in-time 3rd-party test for a fee. We'll capture this in the trust packet.
12:44 Speaker 1 (Jordan): I want to capture the key decisions we just made into action items. Omar, can you confirm procurement committee date is 2026-01-12?
12:51 Speaker 4 (Omar): Yes confirmed.
12:53 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Leah confirm legal wants PHI carveout and a 30-day audit window?
12:58 Speaker 3 (Leah): Correct.
13:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Great. Quick recap of next steps then: Jordan will send annotated MSA+DPA by 2026-01-02, Priya N will send SLA remediation sheet by 2026-01-06, and we'll do a follow-up legal sync on 2026-01-09. Brightwave will confirm approvers and committee date to Jordan by 2026-01-05. Any final comments?
13:20 Speaker 6 (Priya P): Please include subcontractor list and a short statement about APAC personnel access.
13:25 Speaker 7 (Priya N): Will do.
13:28 Speaker 2 (Daniel): Thanks everyone, looking forward to the docs.
13:31 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Thanks all. We'll follow-up with links and the annotated contract. Bye.
13:35 End of recording.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker mis-attribution (Speaker 7 read legal text), minor ASR errors (accents misrecognized), but overall high coverage of key points.
